faq.q: What jewelry photo should I upload?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo of the complete piece on a plain surface. Keep the chain, clasp, stones and setting visible.

faq.q: Can I show how a necklace sits?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a scene that keeps the necklace and neckline in frame. Put the stated length and material in the listing text, not inside the generated image.

faq.q: Which pieces work in a worn photo?
faq.a: Necklaces, earrings, rings, bracelets and cufflinks work when the source shows their shape and finish. If a detail is cut off in the source, it will not be reliable in the result.

faq.q: How do I keep a stone or clasp accurate?
faq.a: Compare the download with the source at full size, and keep only a version whose stone, setting, fastening and color are still recognizable. Reject a frame that invents a prong or changes the metal.

faq.q: Can the worn image sit beside the product listing?
faq.a: Yes. Pair it with the standalone product photo so shoppers see both the piece itself and how it is worn.

faq.q: Do I need to hire a jewelry model?
faq.a: No. The worn scene is generated from your piece photo, so you do not book a hand or a fashion shoot. The person is generated, not a real customer.

faq.q: What does a jewelry photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits, the cost is shown before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your own ads, pages and posts.

faq.q: What if I also need a scene with no person?
faq.a: Use a table or surface scene when scale on a body is not the point. That kind of still is covered by [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos).

steps.prompt: Show an adult wearing the silver necklace at the collarbone, with a light touch on the chain so the size is easy to judge. Keep the pendant and chain in frame, in soft window light.

reviews.lead: A few ways jewelry sellers use one piece photo.

items.d: The shop chooses a neckline scene so a chain's length is easier to judge than on a flat surface. The listing still states the measured length and material.
An earring brand keeps both earrings on a model in a close crop. The source photo stays beside the result, and they keep it only when the metal color still matches.
A hand scene shows the band's width without replacing the plain product photo. The stone and setting are compared at full size before publishing.
The same bracelet photo is used for a wrist scene and a tighter clasp crop. Each run shows its credit cost before it starts.
The worn image goes in the feed, and the plain product photo stays on the product page. Care notes are typed beside the image, not placed inside it.
The team prepares a worn scene from the piece photo they already have. The person or hand is generated, not a booked model and not a customer.
